Apple___Apple_scab.pesticide: Captan, Myclobutanil, or Mancozeb fungicide sprays starting at green tip stage, repeat every 7-10 days during wet periods
Apple___Apple_scab.organic_alternative: Sulfur spray or neem oil applied weekly during wet spring weather
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn, prune for better air circulation, choose resistant apple varieties
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit; leaves may pucker and drop early

Apple___Black_rot.pesticide: Captan 50WP or Thiophanate-methyl fungicide, apply every 10-14 days from bloom to harvest
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Prune infected branches, remove mummified fruit and cankers, improve air circulation
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Circular lesions with concentric rings ('frog-eye') on leaves; black, shriveled fruit rot

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.pesticide: Myclobutanil or Propiconazole fungicide applied from pink bud stage through petal fall
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Remove nearby juniper/cedar trees if possible (alternate host), plant resistant varieties
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on leaves, tube-like structures on the underside

Apple___healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring, balanced fertilization, and proper pruning

Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Maintain acidic soil (pH 4.5-5.5), consistent watering, and mulching

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.pesticide: Myclobutanil or Sulfur-based fungicide at first sign of disease, repeat every 7-14 days
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.organic_alternative: Potassium bicarbonate spray or diluted milk spray (1:9 with water)
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Prune for airflow, avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer, avoid overhead watering
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on leaves and shoots, leaf curling and distortion

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and seasonal pruning

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.pesticide: Azoxystrobin or Pyraclostrobin fungicide applied at first sign of disease, especially before tasseling
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.organic_alternative: Crop rotation combined with copper-based fungicide
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Rotate crops (avoid corn-on-corn), till under crop debris, plant resistant hybrids
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular tan-to-gray lesions running parallel to leaf veins

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.pesticide: Azoxystrobin or Propiconazole fungicide if severity is high before tasseling
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.organic_alternative: Generally minor; sulfur dust for organic control if needed
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids, avoid late planting, ensure good field drainage
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, reddish-brown, elongated pustules scattered on both leaf surfaces

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.pesticide: Azoxystrobin, Propiconazole, or Pyraclostrobin fungicide at early disease onset
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.organic_alternative: Crop rotation and residue management as primary organic control
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Rotate crops, till residue, plant resistant hybrids, avoid dense planting
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical, gray-green to tan lesions ('cigar-shaped') on leaves

Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and balanced fertilization

Grape___Black_rot.pesticide: Mancozeb or Myclobutanil fungicide from early shoot growth through veraison, every 10-14 days
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummified berries and infected canes, improve canopy airflow
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Reddish-brown circular leaf spots; berries shrivel into hard black 'mummies'

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).pesticide: No fully effective chemical cure; trunk injections of fungicide can be used preventatively
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).organic_alternative: Sodium arsenite is banned; rely on cultural control instead
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Prune during dry weather, seal pruning wounds, remove and destroy infected vines
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe pattern of yellow/red streaks between leaf veins, dark spots on berries

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.pesticide: Mancozeb or copper-based fungicide applied every 10-14 days during humid conditions
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Remove fallen leaves, improve air circulation through canopy management
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Dark brown angular spots on leaves that may merge and cause early leaf drop

Grape___healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring, pruning, and canopy management

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).pesticide: No cure exists; insecticides (Imidacloprid) target the Asian citrus psyllid vector to slow spread
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).organic_alternative: Neem oil to manage psyllid populations; remove infected trees
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Control psyllid vector, use certified disease-free nursery stock, remove and destroy infected trees promptly
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy mottled yellowing of leaves, lopsided bitter-tasting fruit, twig dieback

Peach___Bacterial_spot.pesticide: Copper-based bactericide applied during dormant season and early season, oxytetracycline during growing season
Peach___Bacterial_spot.organic_alternative: Copper sulfate spray (use cautiously to avoid phytotoxicity)
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, avoid overhead irrigation, avoid excess nitrogen
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit that may develop into cracks

Peach___healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and seasonal pruning

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.pesticide: Copper-based bactericide combined with Mancozeb, applied every 7-10 days
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use disease-free seed, avoid overhead watering, rotate crops, avoid working in wet fields
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown with yellow halos; scabby fruit lesions

Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and balanced fertilization

Potato___Early_blight.pesticide: Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb fungicide every 7-10 days once symptoms appear
Potato___Early_blight.organic_alternative: Copper-based fungicide or Bacillus subtilis biofungicide
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, avoid overhead irrigation, remove infected debris, ensure adequate plant nutrition
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings ('target' pattern) on older leaves first

Potato___Late_blight.pesticide: Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Metalaxyl-based fungicide applied every 5-7 days in humid conditions
Potato___Late_blight.organic_alternative: Copper-based fungicide applied preventatively before wet weather
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed potatoes, destroy volunteer plants, avoid overhead watering, ensure good drainage
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked pale green to black lesions on leaves, white fungal growth on undersides in humid weather

Potato___healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and crop rotation

Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and cane pruning

Soybean___healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and crop rotation

Squash___Powdery_mildew.pesticide: Myclobutanil or Sulfur-based fungicide at first sign, repeat every 7-14 days
Squash___Powdery_mildew.organic_alternative: Potassium bicarbonate spray or diluted milk spray (1:9 with water)
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Space plants for airflow, avoid overhead watering, plant resistant varieties
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on upper leaf surfaces, spreading to cover entire leaf

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.pesticide: Captan or Myclobutanil fungicide applied at first sign of infection, repeat every 7-14 days
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Remove infected leaves after harvest, avoid overhead irrigation, ensure good air circulation
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Small purple spots on leaves that enlarge and develop scorched, dark red-brown appearance

Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and proper spacing

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.pesticide: Copper-based bactericide combined with Mancozeb, applied every 7-10 days
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.organic_alternative: Copper hydroxide spray, applied preventatively before wet weather
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use disease-free seed and transplants, avoid overhead watering, rotate crops
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, greasy-looking spots on leaves and fruit with yellow halos

Tomato___Early_blight.pesticide: Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb fungicide every 7-10 days once symptoms appear
Tomato___Early_blight.organic_alternative: Copper-based fungicide or Bacillus subtilis biofungicide
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, mulch to prevent soil splash, stake plants for airflow, remove lower infected leaves
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings ('target' pattern) starting on older, lower leaves

Tomato___Late_blight.pesticide: Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Metalaxyl-based fungicide every 5-7 days in humid conditions
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Avoid overhead watering, space plants for airflow, destroy infected plants promptly, avoid planting near potatoes
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large water-soaked gray-green lesions on leaves, white fungal growth on undersides in humid conditions

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.pesticide: Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb fungicide, especially important in greenhouse conditions
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Improve greenhouse ventilation, reduce humidity, avoid overhead watering, space plants adequately
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green-yellow spots on upper leaf surface, olive-green velvety mold on undersides

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.pesticide: Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb fungicide every 7-10 days once symptoms appear
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Remove lower infected leaves, mulch to reduce soil splash, avoid overhead watering, rotate crops
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small circular spots with dark borders and gray/tan centers, tiny black dots visible in center

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.pesticide: Miticide such as Abamectin or Bifenazate; insecticidal soap for lighter infestations
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.organic_alternative: Neem oil spray or release of predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis)
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Maintain adequate humidity, avoid drought stress, monitor regularly for early detection
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling on leaves, fine webbing on undersides, leaves turn bronze and dry

Tomato___Target_Spot.pesticide: Chlorothalonil or Azoxystrobin fungicide every 7-10 days once symptoms appear
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Improve air circulation, avoid overhead watering, remove infected plant debris
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown lesions with concentric target-like rings on leaves, stems, and fruit

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.pesticide: No chemical cure; insecticides (Imidacloprid) to control whitefly vector
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.organic_alternative: Reflective mulch and yellow sticky traps to deter/monitor whiteflies, neem oil
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use virus-resistant varieties, control whitefly populations, remove and destroy infected plants
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of leaves, stunted growth, reduced fruit yield

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.pesticide: No chemical cure; remove and destroy infected plants to prevent spread
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.organic_alternative: Sanitize tools with a milk or bleach solution between plants
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use resistant varieties, disinfect tools and hands, avoid tobacco use near plants, control aphids
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves, leaf distortion, stunted growth

Tomato___healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring and balanced fertilization
